logline: A young weightlifter with Olympic ambitions and a swimming champion reconnect at a sports university, navigating training pressures and first love in a story grounded in athletic reality rather than fantasy.

renewal.note: Single season of 16 episodes, concluded January 11, 2017 on MBC. Inspired by the life of Olympic weightlifter Jang Mi-ran; no continuation planned.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.3 plus a devoted cult following that rediscovered the show on Netflix reflect a consensus that Lee Sung-kyung and Nam Joo-hyuk's chemistry and the drama's refreshingly conflict-lite writing make it one of the best sports romances in K-drama.

pull_quotes.text: Cheerful, sweet and engaging - this show is easy to love.
Nam Joo Hyuk is more melty - and more excellent - than I've seen him, ever.

seasons.review_body: Weightlifting Fairy Kim Bok-joo aired on MBC in late 2016 and early 2017, averaging a modest 4.6% live viewership that nonetheless set up a lasting footprint. The drama found a second life on Netflix as a comfort-watch staple, extending its reach well beyond its initial broadcast numbers. The writing by Yang Hee-seung avoids standard K-drama contrivances, leaving out chaebol heirs and replacing them with low-stakes yet unexpectedly moving tensions around athletic training and young adult self-discovery. Lee Sung-kyung’s Bok-joo stands out as a female lead defined by strength and appetite rather than delicacy, while the chemistry between Bok-joo and Nam Joo-hyuk serves as the show’s main pleasure. The sports setting, inspired by Olympic weightlifter Jang Mi-ran, also gives the romance added credibility.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere introduces Bok-joo with unusual confidence for a K-drama female lead - physically strong, openly emotional, and pursuing a crush with zero self-consciousness. The sports university setting and the initial framing as a friendly rivalry set the show's tone precisely.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bok-joo's first encounter with Joon-hyung in the campus corridor, their old rivalry re-establishing itself before any romance can begin.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale delivers warmth without false stakes. Both leads arrive at their athletic and romantic goals through work and earned growth rather than convenient plot turns. The ending’s quiet satisfaction comes from a drama that trusts its characters throughout.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The resolution of Bok-joo's competition arc - the pay-off of a season's worth of training montages and personal doubt.
